matched: Box plots, EDA, and PPMC applied to 2940 samples from 28 studies (Fig. 2)
Outliers in all groups indicate occasional significant deviations among experiments
Sequencing batch experiments had higher median TIN removal efficiency (78.18%) than continuous flow (74.81%) (Fig. 2(a))
More stable NLR, NiRR, NARR, and NRR observed in sequencing batch experiments
Extremely high NLR, NiRR, NARR, and NRR observed in Du et al. (2016) and Wang et al. (2024b) due to high influent N and short HRT in UASB and EGSB continuous reactors
Difference also observed between floc and aggregate experiments (Fig. 2(b))
High NLR in continuous flow aggregate reactors shows great potential for high-nitrogen wastewater treatment
Synthetic and municipal wastewater had similar effluent properties (Fig. S1(a)) but municipal had more stable rates (Fig. S1(b)) indicating analogous influent properties across studies
Synthetic wastewater had wider ranges of influent COD, NH4+-N, and NO3--N

EDA shows larger distribution regions for municipal wastewater (C/N vs NH4+-N, C/N vs TIN, COD vs NH4+-N, COD vs TIN) (Fig. 2(c), (d)) indicating synthetic influent variables were more concentrated and had less fluctuation
Real municipal wastewater fluctuates greatly, requiring synthetic wastewater experiments to account for real composition/fluctuation
Process types (PNA, PDA, PNA+PDA) showed high differences (Fig. S2), with PNA and PNA+PDA having higher TIN removal than PDA (Fig. S2(a))
Effluent NH4+-N, NO2--N, TIN positively correlated with influent NH4+-N, TIN, NLR across all 3 processes, with strongest correlation (0.55–0.95) in PNA (Fig. 2(e), (f), (g))
PNA requires NOB inhibition and AOB enhancement, which are heavily affected by substrate concentrations (NO2--N, NH4+-N, COD), explaining stronger correlation in PNA
NiRR, NARR, NRR had strong correlations with calculation variables (Text S1)
Influent NH4+-N and TIN had similar pairwise relationships because NH4+-N accounts for >90% of influent TIN in municipal wastewater
PPMC for all variables shows strong relationships between influent type and dominant anammox bacteria, influent NO3--N, and TIN (Fig. S3)
No strong linear relationships between potential inputs except NH4+-N and TIN, avoiding multicollinearity and qualifying them as ML inputs
Variable relationships should be explored further via data-driven and interpretable models
